title: Great Job, Guys!
dateline: The Science Division. The next morning.
mood: Checks in the lab, a race down the stairs, a mop race in the hall, and a warm word from the door.

hero.alt: Seen through the window of a door, Ruby wipes the glass with a cloth while Angela watches from the side and Layla and Fanny sprawl on the shining floor of the hall behind her.

segs.t: Chang’e woke with her cheek on the console. Sun lay across the desk.
The photograph still lay face up beside the empty pudding cup. Mr. Bunny floated by her elbow with a sleeping face on his screen, two flat lines and a small Z.
She had sat up most of the night with the photograph. Somewhere after the founding, she had fallen asleep.
Someone knocked.
Her hand turned the photograph face down before she was properly awake.
“Come in.”

“Good morning, Teacher Chang’e,” said Ruby, in her perfect voice. Angela came in behind her with the doll in the crook of her arm. The watch droid glided in last and stopped by the door, its orange eye lit.
Mr. Bunny’s eyes blinked open. On the console the unsent line about the coil sat where she had left it. Chang’e slid it to the edge and opened a scan.
Angela sat on the lab table with her hands flat on its edge. She had not looked at one instrument. She was looking at the door.
Ruby took a stool by the wall and folded her hands.

Chang’e circled the table with a tablet half her size, Mr. Bunny at her shoulder. She asked the way she would ask a machine: joint torque, sensor reach, cooling. Angela answered each one in a small, careful voice.
On the record Chang’e had watched this same girl strike students with red eyes, a beat late, doing what someone else told her. She did not like the thought. She asked the next question.
“First result,” she said. “An empty socket between her shoulder blades. The Council’s control unit is gone.”
“I pulled it out,” said Ruby. “So she’s safe.”
“So that door is shut. I can’t prove there’s no other.”
Chang’e tapped the tablet. “Her code. That doll. Anything that can receive can be told what to do. She stays on checks.”
Angela’s hands tightened on the table.
A red square blinked on the screen. Forty lines lay hidden under Angela’s walking routines, behind a lock, with a triangle marked DANGER.
“What is this?” said Chang’e.
“Mine,” said Ruby. “It opens to my hand only. It’s a safeguard. If Oro ever takes her again, it lets me stop her.”
Angela looked at Ruby, then away.
“I can’t read it. I can’t open it.” Chang’e typed. “A box only you can open, inside a girl I’m meant to sign off. It goes on the list.”
“Then put me on the list too,” said Ruby sweetly.
“And the doll.” Chang’e held out her hand. “Its left eye is a camera, and it has a live link to Oro. It stays here for checks.”

media.alt: A small doll with pink hair, rabbit-like ears and wide yellow eyes, dressed in a white coat with pink cuffs.

segs.t: Angela folded both arms around it. “No.”
“It’s a camera on a world that wants her back.”
Ruby slid off her stool. “Give it to me.”
Angela looked at her, and gave it. Ruby turned the doll over. Green lines ran from her glove into its back, and a tiny light went out.
“Cut,” said Ruby. “It only sees for her now.”
LINK: NONE, said the tablet. Four seconds. Chang’e had once spent a week cutting a link like that. Ruby put the doll back in Angela’s arms, and Chang’e let her.
The last line of the scan blinked amber. “A fault in your chest,” said Chang’e. “It comes and goes. I can fix it in a minute.”
Angela laid her hand over the place. “Whenever I think about the friends I lost, a malfunction always occurs. But I don’t want to fix this.”
Chang’e’s stylus stopped. “Noted,” she said. She did not fix it.
Mr. Bunny came around to the front of her. Nobody had told him to.
“Fair is fair,” said Ruby. “You’ve read her code. Let me read his.”
His screen went blank.
“Mr. Bunny is my best friend. I won’t let anyone take him away,” said Chang’e.
“I only meant to read him.”
Chang’e heard what she had said. She had said it to the girl whose best friend she had just put on a list.
Beside the lock on her list, she wrote WEEKLY anyway.
Then she took the glove and its dial out of their drawer. Lesley’s hand had been the first in that glove. Lesley had already asked Ruby her question, on the landing lot. That left the needle.
Ruby put her hand in. The glove hummed and lit, and the needle passed the line with room to spare.
Angela’s came last. Whatever drove her shield, the needle read it as aspirant power too.
The same morning.
Layla galloped along the school roof, bent low. Class had started four minutes ago.
Nobody checks the roof,
she thought.
Something landed on her back. She went flat on the tiles.
“Get down, Layla! You’ll be in detention all day if they find you.”
Fanny knelt on her shoulders. Her hip thrusters were still ticking.
“Relax, nobody’s going to find me!” said Layla into the tiles. “Besides...”
She freed one arm and pointed across the roofs at the classroom window.
“If anything, I’ll be in trouble if I don’t hurry to class!” She twisted round. “And you flew up here. Flying is banned.”
Fanny thought about it. “Flying is banned on school grounds. Yes. But if I only sneak in a little flight...”

She sighed and hauled Layla upright. They took the white spiral stairwell at a dead run, each trying to pass the other on the inside. On the last turn their feet crossed. They rolled out into the corridor in a heap.
The classroom door stood open. The teacher waited with arms folded, and every head turned.
“I told you!” Layla threw her hands up. “They’re really going to throw the book at us this time.”
“But at least we’ll be in detention together, hehe!”
She heard it leave her own mouth. Fanny looked at her. Layla studied the ceiling.
Detention was cleaning the Academy hall. Ruby was already there, mopping under the five great stars. The white droid that followed her everywhere stood by the door with its orange eye on her.
“What did you do?” asked Fanny. It was her first detention. She had asked the teacher what to bring.
“I looped my droid.” Ruby leaned on her mop. “I recorded ten minutes of me walking to the library. Then I fed it to the droid’s camera, over and over. It watched that for an hour.”
“And then?” asked Layla.
“I sat in the sun and ate a bun. Nobody followed me. It was wonderful.” She sighed. “Lesley found me on the third bite.”
Angela sat on a bench with her doll in her lap. Nobody had sentenced her. She had come anyway.
“Race you to the far door,” said Ruby, and straddled her mop like a horse.

Layla was off before the word ended. The floor was wet. She slid the last meters on her back. Ruby won, and landed flat beside her, laughing at the ceiling. Fanny came third, after she stopped to set out a wet-floor sign.
“Was it worth it?” Layla asked from the floor. “A bun for a day of mopping?”
“Yes.” Ruby sat up and spun her mop. “To me, home is like a golden birdcage.”
She said it lightly, like a joke. Nobody laughed. Layla thought of the messages from home she had not answered.
On the bench, Angela watched Ruby’s face.
Ruby took a cloth to the window in the side door. Layla and Fanny went down on their knees with floor cloths, side by side. Neither of them said it was a race.
Ruby’s cloth squeaked. On the other side of the glass a face came up into it, round glasses and a grin. Ruby wiped politely around it.
The door opened. Chang’e came out hugging a tablet, Mr. Bunny at her shoulder. Lesley came a full step behind, rifle on her back, her eye on the back of Chang’e’s head.
Layla’s eyes went to the rifle. A coil sat on top of its action, new and bright at the seams. Under it was the old bolt.
Science Division work,
she thought.
I want it in pieces on my desk.
Chang’e stopped in front of them and grinned with her whole face.
“Great job, guys!” she said.

media.alt: Chang'e grins wide in the doorway with a tablet in her arms, and Lesley stands a step behind her in her white officer's coat.

segs.t: Behind her, one corner of Lesley’s mouth moved. On anyone else it would have been a smile. Layla decided it was one.
Then Lesley’s eye moved on and rested on Ruby. The cloth stopped on the glass, halfway through a stroke. The droid’s lens swung from one of them to the other.
Chang’e reached back without looking. She took a fistful of Lesley’s sleeve and towed her level, and on across the hall.
Lesley let her.
Nobody tows Lesley,
thought Layla.
At the far door Chang’e said something up at her. Layla caught one word of the answer.
“No.”
Chang’e did not let go of the sleeve. The door swung shut behind them.
The bell ended detention. Behind the hall, Fanny lay down in the sunny grass and shut her eyes.

media.alt: Fanny lies on her back in the sunny grass in her school uniform, her eyes shut.
media.credit: Official Layla and Fanny lore trailer

segs.t: Layla stood over her. Then she lay down too, an arm’s length away. The grass was warm. That was the only reason.
Ruby had said Oro lay in another galaxy. Fanny had looked up a lot since.
“I wonder if there’s another me on the other side of the sky,” she said.
“I’m not interested in the outside world. I haven’t been sneaking a peek, either,” said Layla, too fast.
Layla did not think about three small leaves under a glass dome.
Fanny raised one hand toward the dome’s pale light and spread her fingers. Layla turned her face aside and watched the hand from the corner of her eye.
